newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares open down, Malaysian OTCs recover.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares open down, Malaysian OTCs recover.

text.p: Singapore shares opened lower on Friday, but Malaysian over-the-counter stocks inched forward as the market took a breather from smart advances by blue chips over the last few days.

"The rises in the Malaysian counters are very selective," said a dealer with a local brokerage. "But the market will continue to trade upwards on index-linked stocks like Cerebos and Fraser & Neave as they are still trading at the year's low."
The key Straits Times Industrials Index fell 2.86 to 2,203.23 after an hour's trade. The UOB OTC index tracking mainly Malaysian shares was up a slight 1.46 points at 1,181.57.
Most dealers said the index would meet strong resistance at the 2,200 level before touching the next support level between 2,250 to 2,300.
The market was mixed, with advancers ahead of decliners by 58 to 50 on thin market volume of 22.37 million shares.

Top active Singapore Telecom 100 continued to trade heavily as small investors who used Central Provident Fund savings to buy shares took profits to meet the September 20 deadline to realise profits in October. Its share remained unchanged at Singapore $3.16.
